cells.tense: What you have been tending is showing up in your hands now, and you can work from plenty instead of from fear of losing it.
cells.act: release the method, not the purpose
cells.ask: Keep the purpose you're devoted to and set down the way you've been carrying it. When the old approach grinds this week, let it go and keep the aim.
cells.core:
Something you tended is arriving, and you're at the door where that happens — the moment when what was outside comes in. You can meet it with your hands open rather than gripped. What comes in can be enjoyed, counted, shared, kept in proportion; you don't have to hold it tight to keep it.

What's arriving may be a thing you're committed to at a new scale, and a way you've been carrying that commitment is sounding tired. Keep the aim, put down the method. That's a release you choose, which is different from one that gets handed to you. Let the grind show you where the commitment is still alive.
cells.sheetLine: What you tended is landing. Nothing has to be held hard.
cells.place: at the door where what was outside arrives

cells.tense: You are already seeing the next harvest before this one is in, and laying plans over ground nobody has walked.
cells.act: meet someone in the middle and go on together
cells.ask: Bring what you've got on one piece of what's arriving to someone who's got their own piece. Meet them there, and carry on from where the two of you land, no clock on it.
cells.core:
The harvest is in and you're already out past it, dreaming the next field before this one is counted. From the door where things arrive, you're running past the arrival, braced for a version of it that hasn't come in yet, and the bracing costs you the actual crop. Plans get laid over ground nobody has walked.

Dreaming works when it's finished with what came before. Pick one person and one offering that's actually arriving, bring what you know, meet what they bring, and go on together from where those two meet. That is one joining, done small, and it puts the vision back on real ground. Care that doesn't clutch is the version of this that breathes.
cells.sheetLine: Bring one thing in before you plant the next field.
cells.place: at the door where what was outside arrives

cells.tense: You are still standing at a door that has already opened, waiting to be told which way to go in.
cells.act: turn toward the one direction and stop surveying
cells.ask: Stop re-checking the other directions. Face the way you keep circling back to, and stay with it a few days — no deadline, no exit held open.
cells.core:
The door where things arrive opened, and you're still on the step, facing backward at a version of your life that's finished there. What's coming in can't get your hands on it while you re-decide a heading you've already chosen. Nothing is arriving because you keep the door in review.

Turn toward the direction you keep circling back to, with no side door held open, and face it this month. Just the heading — not the whole route, not a promise about where it ends. Pick the light you'd move toward without needing proof, and let shining come from what's already been grown. Face one way for a few days.
cells.sheetLine: The door opened. Pick a direction and stop surveying.
cells.place: at the door where what was outside arrives

cells.tense: You are letting one version of your commitment go quiet, and you would say that nothing was ever decided.
cells.act: let the friction test what you are committed to
cells.ask: Pick an aim you'd say you're still holding, do the hard part, and watch what holds — the test only, not a verdict on the rest.
cells.core:
A way you've been carrying something you cared about is thinning, by your own hand. You're not renewing it, and if asked you'd say it just happened. Somewhere in you the matter is open, quietly, while the story says there was a choice you didn't make. The pen is moving and the line at the bottom is blank.

Put a commitment in front of some friction and find out what's real inside it. Pick one aim you'd say you're still holding, do the hard part, and watch yourself. Not a verdict, a test. Whatever the friction shows, you'll have a pen in your hand when you read it.
cells.sheetLine: You're letting something go quietly. Sign the page.
cells.place: at the door where what was outside arrives

attempts.check: The drag on the record is the claim that the harvest now arriving came from the person's own careful tending — the signature says tended fruit is landing, but nothing in the draw says who did the tending, so the core will say what arrives and stop there. A reader could reasonably say the arrival is nothing they planted, or that it is not welcome, and the asks survive that: each one is a small act that teaches something about what they steer by whether or not the reading is right about the garden. The sentence that serves the writer more than the person is 'the garden grown to abundance' — a picture that would flatter the house's map instead of the hand at the table, left out of all four cores.
